question: Plants that are adapted to live under plenty of sunlight are called:
solution:
The correct answer is __**heliophytes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Plants** that are adapted to live under plenty of sunlight are called** heliophytes.**
 
• **Heliophytes **are indeed plants that are adapted to thrive in environments with plenty of sunlight.
 
• They are often found in open areas or at the top of a forest canopy where they can receive maximum sunlight exposure.
 
• **The banyan tree** is a great example of a heliophyte, with its sprawling canopy often dominating the upper layers of a forest.
 
• Heliophytes play an important role in the ecosystem by providing shade, habitat, and food for various organisms, as well as contributing to the overall biodiversity of their environment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Xerophytes** are plants that have evolved to thrive in environments with minimal liquid water, often inhabiting dry habitats like deserts or snow-covered areas.
 
• **Neophytes **refer to plant species introduced into a geographical region in recent history and are not native to that area, while archaeophytes denote non-native plants that have become established in an area over an extended period.
 
• Protophytes, resembling primitive algae, encompass a range of organisms, including unicellular plants, bacteria, yeasts, slime molds, blue-green algae, and various simple green algae.
